## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Upātidhāvanti Sutta* is the ninth discourse of the sixth chapter of the *Udāna* in the Khuddaka Nikāya, cataloged at page 72 of the Pali Text Society edition. The discourse delivers an inspired utterance centered on the imagery of insects flying into the open flames of lamps set out during the night.

Passage-level parallels to the verse are identified across multiple recensions of the *Udānavarga* tradition, specifically corresponding to chapter 29 (the *Yugavarga* or "Day and Night" chapter; Chinese 相應品 / 雙要品) in Sanskrit texts (UV 29, UVS 29), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 29), and Chinese translations in the Taishō canon (T 212.30 and T 213.29).

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
